item.title: Abbas Moves to Reassert Fatah Authority
item.description: The Palestinian president formed a new government, reasserting his authority in the West Bank after Hamas seized power in Gaza.
item.author: ISABEL KERSHNER and TAGHREED EL-KHODARY

item.title: Bus Bombing Kills at Least 24 in Afghan Capital
item.description: The attack was one of the deadliest insurgent strikes in Afghanistan since the fall of the Taliban in 2001.
item.author: BARRY BEARAK

item.title: F.D.A. Tracked Tainted Drugs, but Lost Trail in China
item.description: Two poisoning cases 10 years apart illustrate what happens when nations fail to police the global pipeline of drug ingredients.
item.author: WALT BOGDANICH

item.title: Music Review: Back to a Garden Where More Than Jams Flower
item.description: This year two of Bonnaroo’s three headliners — Tool and the Police — came from way off the jam-band circuit.
item.author: JON PARELES

item.title: Online Sales Lose Steam as Buyers Grow Web-Weary
item.description: Online commerce has enjoyed hypergrowth, but now that growth has slowed sharply in a trend analysts call a turning point.
item.author: MATT RICHTEL and BOB TEDESCHI

item.title: Among Firefighters in New York, Mixed Views on Giuliani
item.description: Some firefighters resent the way the former mayor treated the department before and after Sept. 11.
item.author: MICHAEL WILSON

item.title: The Life of the Chinese Gold Farmer
item.description: How the world of online gaming spawned a multimillion-dollar shadow economy.
item.author: JULIAN DIBBELL

item.title: Move by North Korea to Allow Inspectors Is Welcomed
item.description: Christopher Hill, the U.S. nuclear envoy on North Korea, said that a delegation from the International Atomic Energy Agency was preparing for a trip to North Korea.
item.author: CHOE SANG-HUN
